Hi Kai / Sara —

Thanks for taking the time earlier today. Quick recap from our side and proposed next steps so we keep momentum heading into sizing and a reserved-pool validation:

Summary of what we heard you need (please correct if I missed anything):
- Latency SLOs: p50 <= 30ms, p95 <= 120ms for short sequences (~32 tokens); p95 <= 250ms for streaming flows (avg chunk size 64 tokens).
- Throughput target: sustained 12k tokens/sec across the cluster during peak windows (~200 rps of avg 60 tokens per request).
- Concurrency: burst concurrency up to 120 concurrent requests; baseline active concurrency ~30.
- Streaming requirements: server-side prefix token caching, support for chunked responses with partial commits; want <40ms per chunk beyond first token ideally.
- Security/policy: workload can use Redwood hosted dedicated pool; no sensitive PII needs air-gap today.

Attachments Ive included: helix_sample_trace.json (sample tokenized traces you mentioned), and an initial Redwood GPU comparison spreadsheet to show delta across cards for similar workloads.

Proposed validation plan (short):
1) You send a representative 24-72h tokenized trace (if possible with traffic shape by hour).
2) Redwood runs a 48-hour pilot on two shortlisted HW configs (A100-80 / H100) using your trace with same concurrency profile. We run: native fp16 and int8-quantized inference profiles, both streaming and non-streaming shapes.
3) Deliverables: latency percentile curves (p50/p95/p99), breakdown by sequence length and chunk size, throughput steady-state, and a cost-per-token delta across configs.

Asks from you before we start:
- Confirm we can use the attached helix_sample_trace.json as-is or provide a larger sample.
- Confirm any non-standard tokens/lengths or long-history use cases.
- Approve pilot window (we can start as early as Tue 23 Mar).

Suggested next steps / owners:
- Kai: share final sample trace + peak schedule (Helix)
- Sara: loop in procurement for reserved-pool docs and contract cadence (Helix)
- Karthik (cc): Redwood will prepare the pilot matrix and resource estimate
- Priyom (cc): ops contact for pilot orchestration

If that looks good Ill schedule a 30-minute tech sync to confirm test harness and success criteria (I propose Wed 17 Mar / Thu 18 Mar afternoon PT).

Thanks —

Thanks, Kai & Laura. Ill own the pilot matrix. High-level technical plan below — please review and flag anything missing: 

Pilot matrix (48h each run)
- HW rows: A100-40GB, A100-80GB, H100 (nvlink disabled / enabled variants if you use multi-GPU batching)
- Model variants: fp16 baseline, int8 quant (dynamic range), and a low-latency config that trades off throughput for lower per-token latency (smaller batch windows).
- Workloads: non-streaming (full-response) and streaming (chunked, 64-token chunk size default).
- Traffic shape: replay your supplied hourly profile; include burst windows at +3x baseline for 20-minute intervals.

Key metrics to capture
- p50/p95/p99 latency by sequence length bin (0-32, 33-128, 129-2048)
- tokens/sec sustained and tokens/sec during burst windows
- end-to-end chunk latency for streaming (first byte, per-chunk median)
- KV-cache hit rates and memory pressure (will report swap/evictions)

Back-of-envelope sizing notes (very rough):
- If your steady goal is ~12k tokens/sec and average request is 60 tokens: ~200 rps sustained. For fp16 on A100-80 wed expect ~6-8k tokens/sec per GPU for this model class (depends on sequence distribution). That suggests ~2 GPUs to cover baseline with headroom; add a third for redundancy and peak.
- H100 typically gives 20-30% higher tokens/sec for fp16 and larger improvements for quantized int8 for some kernels; for int8 we expect 9-12k tokens/sec per H100 in similar conditions (again depends on sequence mix). So an H100 reserve might reduce GPU count by ~1 compared to A100-80 for this workload.
- A100-40GB vs A100-80GB: 40GB can limit KV cache for long-context 32k runs; for streaming with many concurrent long histories, wed push to 80GB variants. If you dont use long-context KV heavily, 40GB is viable but requires tighter batching windows.

Proposed immediate deliverable: Ill generate a short CSV estimate (attached) showing 3 scenarios: cost-min, latency-hedged, and capacity-hedged, mapping GPUs, expected tokens/sec, and monthly reserved cost. That will be an input to procurement conversations.

If that looks good well target starting the pilot on Tue 23 Mar. Laura: can you confirm the pilot start window so I can book cluster time?

—Karthik
Head of Platform Solutions, Redwood Inference
